title: Recipe wire validation and typed expression checking maintain drifting call registries
evidence_state: implemented; focused and integration verification passed
problem: recipe.call validation uses a small arity-only callArities allowlist, while expression.inferCall also supports fallback, not, and/or, comparisons, and other typed operations. A change to one registry does not change the other, and an operation accepted by the backend-neutral expression checker can be rejected before it can be persisted as a recipe.
impact: Persisted recipe authors and the existing GraphQL/expression frontend get different operator capabilities and error behavior. New operators can silently become one-frontend-only, making translation/version compatibility hard to reason about.
change: Define a compiler-owned operator capability profile at the recipe boundary: either share the operator/type/arity records with expression checking and lowering, or explicitly version and test the recipe-only subset. Do not claim parity until every documented call has an acceptance/lowering test or an explicit unsupported diagnostic.

review_notes: The persisted-wire validator rejects any call absent from callArities, while the expression checker and physical call renderer accept fallback, not/and/or, comparisons, and contains. BuildRecipePlan reaches expression.Check only after this wire rejection, so the two frontends cannot have parity; the recipe reference also documents fallback as a supported call. This is a source-proven contract mismatch, not merely a table-size preference.

title: Rich-shaping expression validation accepts AST forms that the canonical IR cannot lower
evidence_state: implemented; focused and integration verification passed
problem: Pivot, aggregate, and slice recipe validators accept general expression ASTs through validateExpressionBudget. Semantic rich-shaping lowering then routes pivots, required aggregate expressions, and slice fields through recipeNodeSelector, which rejects every non-selector expression. Catalog pivots are a special omission case, but static pivots and non-selector aggregate/slice expressions are only rejected after the wire validator succeeds.
impact: Invalid persisted recipes survive document validation, can be registered or discovered, and fail later at semantic compilation. Clients cannot know from recipe validation whether a rich-shaping expression is representable, and migration errors occur after a recipe has acquired a durable identity.
change: Make the boundary singular: reject non-selector pivot expressions, required aggregate expressions, and slice field expressions in Bundle.Validate with a stable capability error, or extend the semantic/physical IR and schema to carry them. Add a cross-layer test that validates the same accepted forms it compiles.

migration: Recipes that currently validate but fail rich lowering must be inventoried before tightening validation; migrate them to selectors or a versioned expression representation. Existing valid selector recipes should preserve identity.
review_notes: Pivot and aggregate validators accept general expression ASTs via validateExpressionBudget, and slice fields accept general expressions through the field validator. The semantic rich-shaping boundary then calls recipeNodeSelector for pivot/aggregate selectors and explicitly rejects non-selector slice fields, while the physical lowerers consume selector metadata. Thus a recipe can validate and be registered before a deterministic compiler error; the selector-only intent is stated only in the later semantic comments.

title: Fragment expansion and digesting are not one canonical boundary across resolver, registry, and compiler entrypoints
evidence_state: implemented; focused and integration verification passed
problem: BuildRecipePlan expands fragments before validation and digesting. PersistentRegistry.canonicalEntry also expands and stores a standalone expanded bundle. schema.Resolve and RevisionRegistry.Register validate and digest the original fragment-bearing bundle, then schema.Resolve discovers fields on a clone without expanding fragments. Fragment-based catalog declarations can be missed by direct resolution, and changing fragment expansion policy can invalidate persisted receipts/revision references.

review_notes: BuildRecipePlan expands fragments before validation and digesting. PersistentRegistry.canonicalEntry does the same and stores the expanded bundle. In contrast, schema.Resolve validates and digests the fragment-bearing bundle, then resolves declarations on a clone without expanding fragments; RevisionRegistry.Register also stores/digests the authored bundle.
